what_it_checks: that a request is refused for load only when its priority is negative AND the fleet reports itself fully saturated, and that each queue outcome is translated into the correct caller-visible error

that waiting for capacity blocks for exactly the request's own time to live and then returns a distinct deadline-expired outcome, returns capacity-rejected when nowhere can accept it, and otherwise goes to the least-loaded worker

that the capacity check and the enqueue are atomic, that an over-capacity item is refused rather than queued, that a saturated high band blocks the whole dispatch cycle, and that every item is finalised exactly once including on shutdown

that saturation is the mean of the worse of queue occupancy and memory pressure per target, that a target with missing or stale state scores as fully saturated, that an empty candidate list scores as fully saturated, and that the routing filter fails OPEN by returning the unfiltered list when every target is stale
that every fairness policy honours one shared contract for which workload's queue is served next, distinguishing the shipped boundary-ignoring greedy pick from the starvation-free rotation

that placement runs exclusion then ranking then selection in order, that exclusion short-circuits and errors when it eliminates every target, that each stage receives the previous stage's output, and that out-of-range scores are clamped before weighting
that the highest-scoring targets are returned after a shuffle, so equal scores are resolved non-deterministically: the executable statement that replay is not reproducible

that admission runs before the candidate targets are located, that an empty candidate set and a placement failure produce two DIFFERENT caller-visible statuses, that a failed optional enrichment step does not fail the request, and that the chosen target is recorded
